name: Pike Push-Up
summary: A bodyweight pressing exercise performed in an inverted V-position that targets the shoulders and triceps.

setup: Start in a push-up position with hands flat on the floor slightly wider than shoulder-width.
Walk your feet forward toward your hands while driving your hips up into the air, creating an inverted V-shape with your body.
Distribute your weight onto the balls of your feet and your palms, maintaining a neutral spine and straight legs.
steps: Lower the crown of your head diagonally forward toward the floor by bending your elbows.
Descend until your head gently hovers just above or taps the floor slightly in front of your hands, forming a tripod shape.
Press firmly through your palms to push yourself upward and backward.
Extend your arms fully to return to the apex of the inverted V-position.
instructions.breathing: Inhale as you lower your head toward the floor, and exhale forcefully as you press back up to the starting position.
cues: Form a tripod with your head and hands at the bottom
Keep hips high and pike sharp throughout
Push your head through the window at the top

common_faults.fault: Flaring elbows directly out to the sides.
common_faults.correction: Tuck elbows inward at roughly a 45-degree angle to the torso to protect the shoulder joint.

common_faults.fault: Dropping hips into a standard push-up plane during the movement.
common_faults.correction: Keep your hips high and fixed in the pike position so the pressing angle remains overhead.

common_faults.fault: Lowering the head straight down between the hands instead of forward.
common_faults.correction: Shift your shoulders forward during the descent so your head lands in front of your hands in a tripod pattern.

precautions: Avoid placing excessive direct pressure on the crown of the head upon touching the floor.
Ensure wrists are sufficiently warmed up before loading them in this inverted angle.
